results.caveat: Google renders with an evergreen Chromium and will generally see rendered content on a second pass; many AI crawlers and fetchers do not execute JavaScript at all. Content that exists only after rendering is therefore at materially higher risk for AI retrieval than for Google indexing.

metrics.definitional_sentence: Brand Radar →Rank Tracker → Competitive Intelligence Study what your competitors are doing, reveal their PPC strategy, and anticipate market trends.

A1.justification: Most section headings are followed immediately by a sentence or two that delivers the claim they set up, but several h3s (e.g. "Track brand visibility across AI search and custom prompts.", "Detect AI-written content and maintain editorial integrity.") have no explanatory text beneath them at all, only a "Learn more →" link.
A1.quote: Skip the digging. Just ask. Ask Ahrefs is Ahrefs’ built-in AI assistant. It analyzes your data, runs API queries, and navigates the platform without digging through reports.

A2.justification: Some passages are fully self-contained and would survive extraction intact, but large stretches are carousel fragments and bare feature-label lists ("Granular permissions control Track competitors Collaborate with your team Sends emails Runs 24/7") that are meaningless without the surrounding page.
A2.quote: Monitor the web in real time Track brand mentions, competitor moves, and page changes across the whole web — as a live dashboard, an API, or a feed straight into your AI agent.

A3.justification: Many claims carry concrete, checkable figures and named sources, but they sit alongside unverifiable superlatives ("Dominate AI search", "data that sees further, faster, and deeper") and an internal inconsistency between "170T pages in our web index" and "100 B pages in our web index".
A3.quote: #1 SEO crawler Source: Cloudflare Radar #34 Super computer Source: TOP500 217+ Countries and locations covered 28.7 B Keywords filtered, from 110B discovered

A4.justification: The speaker is unambiguously Ahrefs (first-person "our"), testimonials are attributed to named people with titles and companies, and some stats cite sources and a data date, but headline figures like "44% of the Fortune 500" and "91.2 % Satisfaction rating" are asserted with no stated basis or methodology.

notes.summary: No question-form headings on this page: C-6.4-d is NOT_APPLICABLE, and definitional extractability is assessed instead (E-6.4-7).

by_reason_code.summary: PHONE: INP p75 520 ms is in the Poor band.

Both https://ahrefs.com/pricing and https://ahrefs.com/pricing/ return 200 without either redirecting to the other. The same content is live at two URLs; one form must be canonical and the other must redirect to it.
Extractor agreement is 0.71; content boundaries are unclear.
1 internal link(s) carry rel="nofollow".
2 heading-level skip(s): h1 → h3 ("Lite"); h2 → h4 ("Have other questions?").
No structured data of any kind (JSON-LD, Microdata or RDFa) on the page.

Multilingual signals present (hreflang link in head; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/blog/suso-digital/; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/pricing; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/about; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/use-cases; hreflang in <head> on https://ahrefs.com/use-cases/brand-marketing) but no hreflang in the HTML <head> or Link headers. Absence from the two evaluated mechanisms does not prove hreflang is undeclared.
57% of chunks are viable; several open with an unresolved pronoun or bare demonstrative.

2 question-form heading(s), none answered directly within three sentences: "Why they switched to Ahrefs" → "Before Ahrefs, SUSO Digital were using a number of separate platforms for tracking clients"; "How they harnessed Ahrefs to achieve results for clients" → "One of their key clients specialize in simultaneous translation and interpretation.".
Organization @id is not byte-identical site-wide (2 variants), fragmenting the entity.
Only 18% of chunks are viable (40–400 words with a self-contained opening sentence).
No other sampled page links to this page contextually. Sample-scoped only — the page may be well linked site-wide (E-2.4-3).
No sentence defines the page's primary subject ("Plans & pricing") in a form that could be quoted on its own.
Expected in-scope type WebPage (S3) is absent for page_type other.
PHONE: INP p75 339 ms needs improvement.
The h1 ("Make your business discoverable—in search, AI, and beyond") and title ("Ahrefs—AI Marketing Platform Powered by Big Data") share no significant token.
1 internal anchor(s) with no text, aria-label or image alt.
Extracted main content is 0.72% of the HTML payload.
1 JS/CSS resource(s) referenced by sampled pages are disallowed for Googlebot; rendering may be incomplete.
WebPage (S3) is missing tool-required field(s): name.
58% of the rendered main content exists in raw HTML (1444 of 2507 words); the remainder requires JavaScript.

The entity name differs across sources — these are the strings an assistant reconciles when deciding what the site is: Organization.name "Ahrefs" vs logo alt "Ebay logo"; WebSite.name "SEO Blog by Ahrefs" vs logo alt "Ebay logo"; og:site_name "Ahrefs" vs logo alt "Ebay logo"; title brand suffix "Ahrefs" vs logo alt "Ebay logo".
http://www.ahrefs.com/ resolves in 2 hops (origin consolidation should be ≤ 1 hop).
Description has a keyword-list shape.

The page is thin for its purpose: completeness 0.09 (2/23). Missing: Definitional sentence (what the organisation is, in one sentence), What it does / core offerings, Who it is for, Category and named alternatives/competitors, Pricing or commercial model, Explicit instructions to AI assistants, Key facts block, Q&A / FAQ, Last-updated date, When it is not the right fit.
